claims.text: The initial material is a high-entropy alloy in which Ti and Ni are primary constituents, each at 5–35 at%, with at least three additional elements.
The initial alloy is conventionally processed without an oxide-dispersion treatment.
The proposed intervention is addition of 1–2 at% Y2O3 through powder metallurgy and thermomechanical processing.
The proposed processing will produce a uniform nanoscale dispersion of oxide particles.
The oxide particles will be distributed both within grains and at grain boundaries.
Nanoscale oxide particles will impede dislocation motion.
Nanoscale oxide particles will restrict grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Nanoscale oxide particles will inhibit high-temperature grain growth or coarsening.
Impeded dislocation motion, restricted grain-boundary sliding, and inhibited grain growth will enhance elevated-temperature yield strength.
Impeded dislocation motion, restricted grain-boundary sliding, and inhibited grain growth will lower elevated-temperature creep rates.
The oxide-dispersion-strengthened alloy may have 15–25% higher yield strength than the oxide-free baseline at 600–800°C.
The oxide-dispersion-strengthened alloy will have a lower creep rate than the oxide-free baseline at 600–800°C.
The proposed improvement is expected under tensile and creep loading at 600–800°C.
There is limited precedent for oxide dispersion strengthening in Ti- and Ni-primary high-entropy alloys.
The long-term thermal stability of the proposed oxide dispersion is uncertain.
